fatal_errors: Laser cladding does not reconstruct the target intervention or temperature-dependent indentation/friction study.
The cited evidence concerns an Al-containing HEA coating on AZ91D magnesium and compares it with the bare magnesium matrix, not laser-cladded versus unchanged FeNiCrCoCu coatings on Cu.

The mechanism is only a circular claim that improved microstructure improves wear resistance; it omits dislocation density, HCP fraction, stacking faults, lattice disorder, and the transition above 900 K.
No numerical temperature, velocity, or penetration-depth limits are defined.
The proposed wear test does not specify atomistic or microscopy measurements capable of resolving microscopic deformation.
explanation: The response recognizes the coating/substrate system, proposes a single modification, and names the unchanged coating under identical conditions as a comparator. However, it does not recover the target simulation protocol, the 300–1200 K conditions, or the critical approximately 900 K boundary. Its unconditional improvement prediction conflicts with the target temperature-dependent loss of hardness and wear resistance above 900 K. The laser-cladding citations establish that a different HEA coating can outperform a magnesium substrate, but they do not show that applying laser cladding to an existing FeNiCrCoCu/Cu coating improves it. A discriminating experiment would need matched atomistic sliding/indentation tests while tracking HCP atom fraction, dislocation-line length, lattice disorder, hardness or modulus, tangential force, and friction coefficient across temperature.
